To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of BSs with a wider flat-top amplitude responses leads to a higher number of inter-ring optical band-transfers, and that the use of power-leveling increases this number.

the performance of a direct-detector single-sideband multi-band OFDM metro ring network can be improved by using optical filters with wider flat-top response, when inter-ring band-transfer is performed.

the performance of a direct detection single sideband multi-band orthogonal frequency division multipled metropolitan network when optical filters with non-rectangulare amplitude responses are used for inter-ring band transfer is assessed numerically, and that a maximum number of 30 inter-ring band-transfere are achieved when power-leveling compensation is used.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of BS amplitude response on the maximum number of possible band-transfers, when power-leveling and in its absence.

the performance of a DD SSB-MB OFDM metropolitan network, when different optical band-selectors (with different amplitude response) are used to extract the band of interest for inter-ring band-transfer.
the performance of a DD SSB-MB OFDM metropolitan network when BSs with different amplitude responses and power-leveling are used to perform band-transfer between rings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of optical BSs obtained from real experimental data, with a -3dB bandwidth of 4 GHz, leads to an increase in the number of possible inter-ring band-transfes, in the case that the power-leveling technique is used, and a reduction of the number of possible band-transfers when power-leveling cannot be employed.

the use of BSs with wider flat-top amplitude responses (as opposed to BSs with narrower flat-top amplitude responses) leads to an improvement of the system performance when inter-ring band-transferring is considered, in both cases with and without power-leveling.

the use of BSs with a wider flat-top amplitude (when compared to a 2nd order 4.5-GHz -3-dB super-Gaussian filter), leads to an increased number of inter-ring optical band-transfers, without the need to use power-leveling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the performance of a DD SSB-MB-OFCM metropolitan network employing optical BSs with a flat-top amplitude response is more robust against the number of inter-ring optical band-transfers.
the performance of a DD SSB-MB OFDM metro network is not significantly degraded when optical filters with non-rectangualr amplitude response are used to perform optical band-transfer.

the performance of the DD MB-OFDMA metropolitan network can be improved by using optical band-selectors with a flat-top amplitude response, and by compensating for the BS-induced loss after band-selection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of an MB-OFDM system can be improved by using optical BSs with wider amplitude response.
optical filters with a non-rectangular flat-top amplitude response are beneficial for the performance of band-transfers between DD MB- OFDM metro rings.

optical filters with non-rectangualr amplitude response are required for the implementation of a practical DD MB-OFDMA metropolitan network, in order to achieve a large number of inter-ring-band transfers.
